scenarioCoverage.scenario: A scheduled Sunday run computes a fixed-cutoff snapshot, persists it, renders both report views, publishes, and archives one receipt.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The deterministic test records Compute, Persist, Render, Publish, Archive in order; the archived snapshot ID and receipt snapshot ID match, and Markdown rendering is byte-stable.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use the WR-013 scheduler, in-memory snapshot store, existing Markdown/Telegram renderers, injected publisher transport, receipt service, and the provider-agnostic append-only in-memory archive store.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Telegram delivery fails after one message and explicit retry reuses the same publication.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The first receipt is Partial/Failed with the original snapshot ID; retry succeeds at attempt two and the transport receives the exact same chunks in the same order.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Inject a one-shot failure at a later chunk, inspect the typed failure, retry the retained service, and compare all recorded payloads.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: No structural change produces an explicit no-change Markdown/Telegram output without fabricated sections.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The full Markdown and short Telegram view contain the explicit No Change statement, and the Telegram output has no Top5/Rising/Dropped sections.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Build empty WeeklyChangeCompression and NoChangeSummary inputs and assert stable output across two renders.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The CI workflow uses the latest requested checkout action.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The workflow has exactly two actions/checkout@v5 references, one per job, and zero actions/checkout@v4 references.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Read the repository workflow as a test fixture and assert exact version counts and absence of the stale version.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: External delivery and secret safety remain isolated from E2E verification.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The test uses fixed values and an in-memory transport; no Telegram token, chat ID, HTTP client, or external network call appears in the E2E path.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use source inspection and deterministic fakes, then run the architecture and secret-safety checks.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record the full E2E/workflow scope before edits and the final cross-boundary verification before Finish.

acceptance: The repository workflow has two actions/checkout@v5 references and no actions/checkout@v4 reference; both jobs retain checkout depth 0.

A public E2E test composes the Scheduler, supplied-cutoff WeeklyRadarSnapshot, append-only SnapshotStore, Markdown renderer, Telegram renderer, semantic splitter, injected Telegram publisher, PublicationReceipt, and the append-only in-memory WeeklyRadarArchive.
The success path proves Compute → Persist Snapshot → Render → Publish → Archive order, stable Markdown output, matching snapshot/receipt identity, and an archived Published receipt.
The failure path proves a typed partial delivery result, unchanged snapshot identity, explicit retry at attempt two, and byte-identical ordered Telegram payload reuse.
No-change and external-isolation scenarios pass without real network access, credentials, secrets, provider SDKs, production timers, or persisted scheduler state.
Focused E2E tests, full repository quality, strict Finish/Archive, PR checks, merge, close, and branch cleanup pass with the authorization recorded in the Contract.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.
Keep E2E orchestration in tests; the Archive boundary may retain only supplied snapshot/receipt values and must not add external persistence merely to make the test pass.
Use fixed timestamps, cutoff values, facts, and in-memory transports; never use Telegram credentials or real network calls in tests.
Treat the existing WI as the repair boundary for defects discovered here; do not create a new WI unless the change is outside this E2E/workflow scope.
Keep actions/checkout@v5 in both workflow checkout steps and do not reintroduce @v4.

intent.problem: The Weekly Radar components now exist as separately verified boundaries, but no single deterministic test proves the ordered weekly flow from Scheduler through Snapshot, Markdown/Telegram rendering, Receipt-aware publication, retry, and Archive. The CI workflow also still uses actions/checkout@v4 despite the required latest checkout@v5 correction.
constraints: Compose existing production boundaries in a public integration test; keep Archive storage append-only, in-memory, provider-agnostic, and free of external database behavior.
Use a supplied evidence cutoff and snapshot identity, explicit no-change facts, injected clocks/transports, and no real network or provider configuration values.
Prove Compute → Persist Snapshot → Render → Publish → Archive ordering and prove retry resends the same immutable publication rather than recalculating.
Change only the two workflow checkout references from @v4 to @v5; keep fetch-depth and quality commands intact.
Complete TDD, focused/module-local/integration verification, strict Finish/Archive, local commit, publish, merge, close, and branch cleanup under the recorded lifecycle.
intent.rationale: One deterministic end-to-end seam turns the already-built local boundaries into an auditable weekly execution contract and prevents CI action drift while preserving sensitive provider configuration and provider isolation.
